business_rules.ears: WHEN posting an entry THE SYSTEM SHALL drop zero lines AND refuse the entry unless total debits equal total credits and are above zero; a deferred Postgres constraint trigger SHALL re-check at commit.

business_rules.description: Who owes me is the ledger, not invoice status.
business_rules.ears: WHEN showing what a customer owes THE SYSTEM SHALL sum receivable debits minus credits on lines tagged with that customer, and SHALL list customers whose balance is non-zero.

business_rules.description: GST to pay is payable minus input for the month.
business_rules.ears: WHEN showing GST for a month THE SYSTEM SHALL compute *_payable credits minus *_input debits for entries dated in that month, less unused credit carried from earlier months, AND SHALL show one overall 'GST to pay' figure with the CGST/SGST/IGST breakdown below; a negative figure SHALL show as credit carried forward.

business_rules.description: Profit is revenue less expenses from the ledger, by document date.
business_rules.ears: WHEN showing profit for a month THE SYSTEM SHALL take revenue credits minus debits less expenses debits minus credits for entries dated in that month, with expenses split by the category of the bill that posted them.

WHEN showing /stats THE SYSTEM SHALL leave out workspaces flagged as team AND count as people only workspaces that saved an invoice or bill today (IST); invoices, bills, reminders and ₹ invoiced exclude team workspaces too.

open_questions.plain: Does the GST credit actually carry forward?
open_questions.question: A negative month is labelled 'credit carried forward', but gstForMonth only looks at one month; next month starts from zero and the credit is lost from the number. Carry the prior balance in, or relabel it as 'more GST paid than collected this month'?
evidence: src/lib/books.ts gstForMonth filters to one month
open_questions.resolution: Carry it forward. GST to pay for a month subtracts unused input credit left over from earlier months, shown as its own line.

open_questions.plain: Two views, or a books page?
open_questions.question: README and SPEC say the books show as two views only. b377a53 added /books with profit, balances and the journal. Which is the story for judges: 'two plain views' (simple), or 'real books you can inspect' (credible)? It changes the demo and the deck.
evidence: README.md 'They show as two views only'
open_questions.resolution: Simple first, proof behind. Home shows the plain views (owed, GST, profit). /books is one tap deeper as proof of real double entry. The demo shows the plain view, then flashes the balance check.

open_questions.plain: Net GST per head, or overall?
open_questions.question: The view nets CGST, SGST and IGST separately and also gives an overall net. Under GST set-off rules IGST credit can pay CGST and SGST, but CGST credit can't pay SGST. A per-head negative next to a positive overall is confusing. Show only the overall today and leave set-off for GSTR-3B in Month 3?
open_questions.resolution: One overall number: big 'GST to pay ₹X' (or credit), with CGST/SGST/IGST in a small breakdown below. Statutory set-off order comes with GSTR-3B in Month 3.

open_questions.question: Profit is accrual: revenue counts when the invoice is issued, not when paid, and bills count when dated. A freelancer may read 'you made ₹X' as cash in hand. Keep 'profit', or say 'billed less spent' and add cash received later?
open_questions.resolution: Keep 'Profit this month' and add a line under it: 'Money in: ₹X actually received' (bank and clearing debits from payments that month).

open_questions.plain: How do we fix a wrong entry?
open_questions.question: The ledger is append-only with no reversal. Any fix to an invoice or bill (intent-invoicing OQ-INV-3, intent-bills OQ-BIL-5) needs a reversing entry type. Add source_type 'reversal' when one of those is decided.
open_questions.resolution: Yes. OQ-INV-3 adds Cancel invoice, so the ledger gets source_type 'reversal': an entry that mirrors the original with debits and credits swapped.

open_questions.plain: Is TDS 10% of the fee before GST, or the whole total?
open_questions.question: TDS under 194J is on the fee excluding GST when GST is shown separately. So on ₹40,000 + ₹7,200 GST, TDS is ₹4,000, not ₹4,720. Confirm the 'paid less TDS' option uses 10% of the subtotal, and whether 2% (194J technical services) or 1%/2% (194C contracts) also need offering.
open_questions.resolution: One option: 'Paid less 10% TDS', computed on the subtotal (fee before GST). Other rates later.
